title: Guardrail orchestration metrics and explainability
content:
Purpose and intent:
This note captures the runtime design, telemetry surface, and explainability log format for the platform-side policy/evaluator used by routing, model-selection, and guardrail decisions across multi-region Redwood deployments. Aim: produce an operationally lightweight evaluator that supports hard constraints, prioritized soft constraints, quantitative scoring, and deterministic explainability artifacts suitable for debugging, audits, and ML-driven regressions.

Context and constraints:
- This evaluator sits in the control plane request path (pre-routing) and as a local policy-check in the serving runtime (for per-node fast fallbacks).
- Requirements: sub-ms median decision time for common cases, deterministic outputs for identical inputs, bounded memory per-request, and compact explainability logs that can be sampled and stored for 30–90 days depending on SLA.
- Multi-region nuance: many rules are region-specific (data sovereignty, model licensing). Policy data is versioned and can be pinned per-tenant.

Data model for constraints and scopes:
- Constraint record (compact, protobuf-compatible): id, kind, scope, priority, expression, params, region_set, version_tag.
- Kind: HARD | SOFT | META (e.g., deprecation notices).
- Scope: GLOBAL | TENANT:<id> | ROUTE:<route_id> | NODE_POOL:<pool_id>. Scopes are evaluated in order of specificity (node_pool -> route -> tenant -> global).
- Priority: integer (higher => more important). Hard constraints with conflicting scopes are resolved by highest priority; conflicts among same-priority hard constraints are a policy definition error surfaced to control-plane audit.
- Expression language: small, typed DSL (operators: in_set, not_in_set, regex_match, numeric_cmp, latency_estimate_cmp). Expressions are precompiled to bytecode in the control plane for fast evaluation in the runtime.

Scoring and ranking model (high level):
- Purpose: when multiple soft constraints / routing preferences apply, produce a single numeric score used by the router and for fallback ordering.
- Score composition: score = base_score + sum_i weight_i * normalized(metric_i) + penalty_terms. All components normalized to [-1,1], final score clamped to [-100,100].
- Metric examples: estimated_token_cost, tail_latency_percentile, model_quality_delta (from evaluation service), freshness_penalty (how stale a model is relative to pinned version).
- Weight assignment: default weights live in the control plane config; tenants can override a subset via policy profiles. Weights are versioned and validated against a schema.
- Determinism: scoring uses deterministic tie-breaker (policy_version + request_id hashed) to avoid oscillation in equal-score cases.

Explainability log design (goals):
- Compact, structured, and human-readable. Must enable: root-cause for a routing decision, audit trails for constraint enforcement, and inputs for ML offline analyses.
- Stored as JSONL in a compressed telemetry store; sampled using both rate and event-type triggers (e.g., every 1k requests + all constraint-violation events).
- Fields captured (flat schema only): request_id, timestamp, control_plane_version, policy_snapshot_id, tenant_id, route_id, selected_model_id, final_score, decision_reason, hard_constraints_triggered (comma-separated ids), soft_constraints_applied (comma-separated ids), score_breakdown (semicolon-separated key=val pairs), latency_budget_ms, region, node_pool, eval_duration_ms, sampling_flag.
- Example line (single-line JSON): {"request_id":"r-3f9a", "timestamp":"2025-02-27T14:03:10Z", "control_plane_version":"v2.11.0", "policy_snapshot_id":"ps-20250227-7", "tenant_id":"t-435", "route_id":"/generate", "selected_model_id":"gpt-open-3b-quant", "final_score":"73.4", "decision_reason":"passed_hard_constraints_then_highest_score", "hard_constraints_triggered":"c-101,c-219", "soft_constraints_applied":"c-532,c-401", "score_breakdown":"base=50.0;cost=-2.1;latency=12.5;quality=12.0;freshness=1.0", "latency_budget_ms":"120", "region":"eu-west-1", "node_pool":"np-gpu-p2", "eval_duration_ms":"0.7", "sampling_flag":"rate" }

Runtime flow (fast path + slow path):
- Fast path: control plane returns a compact policy snapshot (TTL ~60s) to edge nodes; nodes evaluate only the minimal set of constraints required for routing (pre-compiled expressions + cached context such as tenant profile). Typical eval <1ms.
- Slow path: when policy snapshot is stale or a new tenant scope is added, node issues policy fetch and does a blocking re-eval; log entry marked sampling_flag="fetch".
- Local fallback: if node runtime detects a model is unhealthy (heartbeat or tail latencies), it triggers the policy evaluator with an adjusted context (model_unhealthy=true) to pick next-best compatible model.

Interaction with control plane and snapshots:
- Control plane responsibilities: authoring UI, policy versioning, snapshot generation, validation (schema + semantic checks), and push strategy (long-poll + delta patches).
- Snapshot contains: policy_manifest (list of constraints + metadata), weight_profiles, region_overrides, allowed_model_sets per-tenant, snapshot_id, created_at.
- Delta patches encoded as sequence of add/remove/modify ops to minimize bandwidth. Nodes must be able to apply patches idempotently.

Multi-region considerations and data sovereignty:
- Region_set on constraints restricts applicability; evaluation short-circuits for mismatched regions to reduce work.
- Some policy clauses are conditional on data residency (e.g., forbidding cross-region models for PII routes). Such clauses are declared HARD with explicit region tags.
- Rollout ordering: control plane prefers local-region first, then regional-fallback pools, then global when allowed by constraints. This ordering is part of the default weight_profile.

Operational telemetry and SLOs:
- Key metrics emitted per-eval: eval_latency_ms (p50/p95/p99), constraints_evaluated_count, hard_violations_count, soft_applied_count, explain_log_emitted (count), policy_snapshot_age_seconds.
- SLOs: median eval_latency < 1ms on edge nodes; p99 < 10ms. Snapshot apply success rate > 99.9% over 30d. Explainability write success > 99% for sampled events.
- Alert rules: sudden spike in hard_violations_count, or policy_snapshot_age_seconds > 120s for >5m should page platform oncall.

Failure modes and mitigation:
- Stale snapshot: node should fall back to previous snapshot and mark explainability entry sampling_flag="stale_snapshot"; control plane page if a region-wide staleness persists.
- Conflicting hard constraints: control plane validation prevents this for active snapshots. If detected at eval time (should be rare), evaluator rejects request with a safe default (deny-by-default) and emits high-severity audit log.
- Telemetry loss: explain logs are buffered in memory with bounded queue; if queue fills, logs are dropped with incrementing counter exposed to alerts.

Extensibility notes and next actions:
- Short-term (next sprint): add a compact bitset encoding for hard_constraints_triggered to reduce log size and enable fast offline filters. Implement a lightweight deterministic sampling strategy that biases towards newly-created policy_snapshot_ids.
- Medium-term: move scoring weights into a learnable online store while keeping a fail-safe static profile; run A/B tests for weight changes using rollout framework.
- Long-term: expose a tenant-facing explainability endpoint (redwood-managed) that surfaces filtered logs for audits under access controls.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- How long should explainability logs be retained for enterprise vs hosted tiers? (30/90/365 day options?)
- Do we allow tenant-specified weight overrides for model_quality_delta in hosted plan? security/compliance implications.
- Finalize DSL grammar to ensure no Turing-complete constructs are allowed.

Notes-to-self / links for follow-up:
- See control plane spec draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PLAT/Policy+Runtime+Spec
- Related Git PR for snapshot delta encoding: https://git.redwood.ai/platform/pulls/431
- Audit ticket template: JIRA-PLAT-987

End of note.
